summary: Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. from Case Western Reserve University in 2001 under Melvyn C. Goldstein. As of 2008, he served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Ben Joffe works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Colorado Boulder, where he completed his Ph.D. under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

Benedetta Lomi works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, holding a PhD from SOAS University of London. Her career includes a fellowship at UC Berkeley (~2011–2012), an assistant professorship at the University of Virginia (~2012–2018), and a lectureship at the University of Bristol (~2018).

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an MA at the University of Calcutta and a D.Litt. at the University of London. He served as a lecturer (1913–1914) and professor (1918–1948) at the University of Calcutta.

Benjamin A. Elman is a historian and sinologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He was a professor at UCLA (1986–2002) and became Director of Princeton University's East Asian Studies Program in 2002.

Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also studied under Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his Ph.D. from Stanford University (~2004–2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and was an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2010–2016).

Benjamin C. Ray is a religious studies scholar. He served as the Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at the University of Virginia, where his faculty affiliation is attested in 2000 and 2026.
Benjamin Fleming is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the City University of New York (attested 2021).
Benjamin Goldstein is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. As of 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.

Benjamin Lewis Rice (1837–1927) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Director of Public Instruction in Mysore and Coorg (~1868–1883) and as Director of the Mysore Archaeological Department (~1884–1889).
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University and Harvard University (~1992–1996) and held a post at the University of Michigan around 2004.

Benjamin Wood is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Toronto under the supervision of Frances Garrett, also studying under Shayne Clarke, Thubten Champa, and Khenpo Kunga Sherab.

Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo (~1910–1915). He was president of Taisho University (1926), first president of Tokai Gakuen University Junior College (1963), and headed the Sanko Research Institute (~1948–1971).

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka. He served as General Editor of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (1924) and Director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1927–1952).

Benoît Vermander is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who holds doctorates from Sciences Po and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and became a professor of religious sciences at Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned his Doctorat d'État from the University of Paris. He taught at Cornell (~1983–1987) before holding professorships at Stanford (~1987–2006) and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank (1927–1996) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernard Goldman (1922–2006) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1950–1955) and held an academic post at Wayne State University (~1956–1987).

Bernard Williams (1929–2003) was a philosopher who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He held academic posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).
